text:
🇲🇾The Full 2D1N Malacca Trip Itinerary | just copy & paste it! 

This time we took a bus from Larkin,
and reached Melaka in around 3+ hours 🚍

Round trip tickets were about RM50 per person,
really suitable for a short weekend getaway.

For accommodation, we stayed at Hatten Hotel Melaka,
and the location was honestly very convenient.
Most attractions were within walking distance.

📍Jonker Street
The vibe during the day and night feels completely different 😳

🌅 In the daytime,
it’s more chill and relaxing.
There are lots of old shops, cafes, and small hidden stores,
perfect for slow walking and taking photos.

🌃 At night,
the whole street becomes super lively ✨
Lights, trishaws, food stalls, music, and crowds —
the travel vibe feels so strong.

We also visited:
📍Stadthuys (must visit)
📍Flor de la Mar Maritime Museum (can go inside)
📍A Famosa (can explore)
📍Malacca River riverside walk

Most of the attractions are actually quite near to each other,
so you can slowly walk around and explore everything comfortably.

One unexpected find was:
📍Hiyori by Young Look

We originally just wanted to go in for air conditioning 😅
but the whole place felt like a Japanese-style eyewear shop.

A lot of their frame designs
are styles we rarely see in Singapore or Johor Bahru.

The space was really comfortable too,
almost like a small Tokyo boutique.

For food, we tried:
🍢 McQuek’s Satay Celup (must eat)
🍰 Nadeje mille crepe cake (must eat)
🥮 Nyonya kuih
🎁 San Shu Gong souvenirs

Especially the Satay Celup —
the longer it cooks, the more fragrant it gets 🤤
It feels even better eating it at night.

If you’ve been wanting a short escape recently
but don’t want to take too much leave,

Melaka really is a great choice for a 2D1N trip ✨
